name: Softfil

card.summary: SoftFil is a brand of microcannula that clinicians use to place hyaluronic acid fillers, for example to build the chin or smooth the under-eye area.
card.note: Filler injections are clinical procedures with documented vascular and bruising risks.

quick.overview:
SoftFil appears in the aesthetic literature as a blunt-tipped microcannula used to deliver filler instead of a sharp needle. Clinicians use it to place hyaluronic acid or similar injectables for chin, cheek and tear trough work.

The appearance payoff comes from the filler it delivers: a fuller chin, restored cheek volume or smoother tear trough. Published reports are small case series and single cases, not large trials.
quick.how: The procedure is performed by a clinician, who enters at a small number of points and threads the cannula through the tissue layers. Results are visible after swelling settles and are followed at weeks to months in studies.
quick.risks: Fillers cause bruising, redness and swelling. Rare serious complications such as vascular occlusion are documented for fillers generally. Procedures belong with trained clinicians.

lead: SoftFil is a cannula brand that appears in published reports of facial filler treatment. A 2024 study of 40 women with a small chin used a SoftFil cannula to place Revanesse Versa hyaluronic acid filler in three entry points and several layers; satisfaction rose significantly at 14 days and was maintained to six months.[1]

In another report, five women aged 35 to 50 had the tear trough treated with a polynucleotide product (VAMP) using a SoftFil microcannula, with mild to moderate improvements and no adverse events in three months, though the authors note small size and short follow-up.[2] A 2021 case compared a SoftFil cannula and a needle under ultrasound and found both could reach the supraperiosteal plane in the malar and chin areas.[3]
Wikipedia notes that hyaluronic acid fillers last about six months depending on product and provider, and describes bruising, lumps and, rarely, blindness from vessel blockage.[4]

chain: Clinician places filler through a microcannula
Chin, cheek or tear trough volume increases
Face contour looks fuller and smoother
angle.text: The cannula is the delivery tool for filler, which adds volume to the chin, cheeks or under-eye area. Reported results last months.

infobox: Hyaluronic acid and other injectable fillers

paras: A cannula has a blunt tip and is inserted through a small entry point, whereas a needle is sharp. The 2021 ultrasound comparison tested whether a SoftFil cannula could reach the periosteum like a needle.[3]

The three-point chin study followed 40 women to six months with high satisfaction.[1] The tear trough report included five patients with no adverse events over three months.[2] The 2021 case used one patient and ultrasound.[3] All are small, uncontrolled reports.
Common filler effects include bruising, redness, pain and itching; less common are infection, allergy, scarring and lumps, and rarely blindness from embolization.[4]
